verdict.tagline: Portal meets arena shooter, but official servers are offline.

cohorts.summary: Reviewers praise the arena shooter gameplay combining portal mechanics with smooth performance and a free model.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a free model with no in-app payments and unlockable skins/models provided through challenges and gameplay.

citations.review_text:
It is the first game I see that does not have in-app payments and there are a variety of skins and models, all for free, and there is no need to try anything like leveling up.
The graphics of the game are very good, one of the best games for photography.
The gameplay of the game was a new experience for me (portal online).
The question is, what profit did the developer make despite the entire game being free?!

People weren’t lying: This is the Halo with portals. After 25 hours of Splitgate 2 and only 30 minutes in Splitgate, I noticed how it’s better than its successor in almost every way, including true-to-core arena maps and the simplicity of shooting.

And the best thing of all is that the game rewards you with a bunch of skins if you play well and complete certain challenges, as it should.

Edit: And the servers are gonna get killed so the sequel can survive... I hope they somehow turn the tide around.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance as smooth and well-optimized, maintaining around 120 FPS on older hardware like an RX 480.

citations.review_text:
Splitgate is what happens when Halo and Portal have a beautiful child, and that child grows up to punch you in the ego at 120 FPS.

At first you’re like, “Cool! I’ll place portals for smart flanks!”
Then you realize everyone else is placing portals for **quantum assassination**. You’ll be calmly holding an angle and suddenly get shot in the back by a person who entered the room through a wall like it was a suggestion.

The gunplay is crisp, the movement is smooth, and the portal mechanics turn every map into a 4D chessboard. Except you’re playing checkers. With one piece. And it’s on fire.

Also: the *moment* you start feeling confident, you’ll try a fancy portal play, accidentally put your exit portal directly in front of an enemy, and essentially hand-deliver yourself like an Amazon package labeled “FREE KILL.”

**Pros:**

* Fantastic FPS feel
* Portals make every match creative and chaotic
* Outplays are insanely satisfying

**Cons:**

* Learning curve is shaped like a wall you can’t portal through
* I have been bullied by angles I didn’t know existed
* “Where did he come from?” becomes your catchphrase

10/10. Splitgate made me feel like a tactical genius, then immediately reminded me I’m a very confident snack for portal wizards.
fun and well optimized 120ish fps for my rx 480

claims.claim: Reviewers compare the gameplay to a combination of Portal and Halo.

citations.review_text:
[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
In the end what I will remember this game for was filling a Halo-shaped hole in my heart in the weeks before the Halo Infinite launched. Sadly Infinite went down the tubes a few months after, and now that Halo-shaped hole has been carved and filled with THE FINALS and I've never looked back.

The game is worth checking out if it sounds if the premise sounds interesting to you.

[h2] Thoughts from my hed [/h2]
Ultimately I can't recommend it. I am not sure if the servers are up anymore- splitgate 2 may still exist depending on when you read this. But based on what I've played there, it hasn't made any meaningful improvements and in some cases cheapened the experience.

The game is fun enough to play, but the main thing I don't like about this game is how it necessitates the portal play more than it does FPS skill. Don't get me wrong, I think portals can absolutely work in an FPS space and be really interesting. 

I'm not going to spend too much time thinking about it, but what it comes down to is that Splitgate devs don't have a tight design vision for this game. It comes off more as two fun and accepted ideas slapped together (Portal and Halo) and doesn't look much beyond that. The rough edges show in the design- fights are primarily fought through shifting (blind) sightlines and a revolving cat-and-mouse style of combat. It is fun, but it doesn't have staying power to me because of the aforementioned lack in design vision and an uncontrolled scope.

👍 Recommended? Portal + Halo should never have worked. It somehow became one of my favourite shooters ever made.

Whoever looked at Halo and Portal and said,
"Let's combine them."

deserves a raise.

The skill ceiling wasn't high.

It was in orbit.

You weren't getting out-aimed.

You were getting shot through three portals by someone with the spatial awareness of NASA.

Every killcam looked illegal.

Meanwhile I was accidentally portaling myself directly into the enemy team for the eighteenth time.

Splitgate never took itself too seriously.

It was just pure fun.

No billion-dollar live service strategy.

No twenty-seven currencies.

Just portals, ridiculous plays, and "HOW DID HE GET THERE?"

I miss it.

If you enjoyed Portal
But you also wanted to shoot people like Halo

Welcome to Splitgate.

citations.review_text: Fresh merging of Portal and Halo

The most fun I've had in a shooter since Titanfall 2. It feels so good to be good at this game. Extremely satisfying to play with smooth, seamless movement. It feels like a classic old school arena shooter. It is the perfect mix of halo with portals. It's clear from the maps and guns that it takes a lot of insipiration from halo but this game had a clear personality that was awesome. 

Unfortunately this game is fully dead in the water due to the devs completely pulling the pin on this game to create a 2nd inferior one that they will also then pull the pin on early in the games lifecycle to chase a quick cash grab and hopefully boom overnight with Empulse. The devs can go to hell for ruining a unique game that filled a fun niche within the shooter market

The servers have shut down, but peer-to-peer custom lobbies remain, which can be either public or private with a password. All players also now have access to all the cosmetic items for free. Although the complete lack of matchmaking now makes it difficult to experience it as it originally intended, Splitgate gives an excellent example of doing end of life plans for a live service game right.

I would have had trouble recommending this before due to its predatory battlepass and microtransactions systems, but now this is a non-issue due to the servers no longer being live.

As for the game itself, Splitgate is literally Halo but with a portal gun, and it is super fun! Place portals to quickly get around the map, to fling yourself, or to flank enemies. Someone is sniping you from across the map? Out-gunning you in a corridor? Catch them off guard by placing a portal behind them and shooting them in the back (nothing personal, kid). Died and want to get back into the action? No need to walk, portal right back into the action. The gunplay and portals are very well designed. The gameplay is very satisfying and makes you feel awesome. The graphics look great while still having high framerates, even even with being able to see through your portals.

It is well worth downloading if you have friends to play with, or if you are lucky enough to find a good player-hosted public lobby.

At least add community/P2P servers.
